title: Beyond Success Rate: Interventional Evaluation of Memory in Vision-Language-Action Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.23372v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: When we say that a robot uses memory, does that memory actually play a role? Success-rate ablations alone cannot establish the use of task-relevant facts: they change information and computation together, while aggregate rates can hide offsetting gains and losses. We propose an Interventional Memory Evaluation Protocol (IMEP) for vision-language-action (VLA) systems to address four questions: (1) Does memory provide a net benefit? (2) Under what conditions does memory help? (3) Do changes to memory alter task outcomes? (4) Are these effects specific to task-relevant facts? At the retrieval interface, we compare target-fact substitutions with fact-preserving replacements, minimal numerical perturbations, and exact replicas, while assessing decision correctness separately from motor execution success. translated_abstract: 当我们说一个机器人使用了记忆时，这段记忆是否真的发挥了作用？仅凭成功率的消融实验无法确立对任务相关事实的利用：这类实验在改变信息的同时也改变了计算，而总体成功率可能掩盖相互抵消的收益与损失。我们提出了一种面向视觉-语言-动作（VLA）系统的干预性记忆评估协议（IMEP），以回答四个问题：(1) 记忆是否带来净收益？(2) 在什么条件下记忆有帮助？(3) 对记忆的改动是否会改变任务结果？(4) 这些效应是否特定于任务相关的事实？在检索接口处，我们将目标事实替换与保留事实的替换、最小数值扰动以及精确副本进行比较，同时将决策正确性与运动执行成功率分开评估。我们评估了回合内记忆、跨回合记忆以及智能体式记忆。在跨回合学习库实验中，一个末位单位（UL……
tldr: 该论文提出干预性记忆评估协议（IMEP），通过目标事实替换等干预操作并将决策正确性与执行成功率分开评估，以严格检验记忆在视觉-语言-动作系统中是否真正发挥作用。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes an Interventional Memory Evaluation Protocol (IMEP) that uses targeted fact substitutions and separates decision correctness from motor execution success to rigorously test whether memory actually plays a role in vision-language-action systems.
